messages:
incidents-bot: 🔔 ALERT: p99_streaming_latency > 10s in cluster dedicated-us-west for service /v1/stream (threshold 7s)

oncall-jen: taking this. tagging @sre-liam and @runtime-alejandra. any customer-visible errors?

sre-liam: seeing p95 ~ 2.3s, p99 ~ 12.6s on the dashboards. queue depth for dedicated-us-west jumped from ~30 -> 120 over the last 3m. streaming stalls visible on tail router (many requests stuck in WAIT_FOR_POOL).

runtime-alejandra: streaming stalls correlate with pool allocation delays — autoscaler shows several pool spinups stuck in WARMUP for >60s. warmup success rate dropped.

product-mike: are we seeing any fallback to smaller models? might minimize impact for PLG customers. enterprise tenants on reserved capacity flagged by CS.

customer-success-sara: two critical customers reported timeouts in the last 10m (tickets #7812, #7813). both on dedicated us-west. CCed engineer contacts. They see streaming stalls and aborted connections.

infra-ops-bot: autoscaler event: pool-create request 6250001210 id=pc-84f2 pending_warmup; healthchecks failing: failed_init=3/3; warmup_duration=78s.

oncall-jen: mitigation plan - 1) divert non-critical PLG traffic to hosted fallback 2) manually scale additional hotshot pool 3) evict low-priority background jobs to free slots. executing step 1 now.

sre-liam: step 1 done — traffic rule applied: route tags (~plg) -> hosted-fallback for 10m. expected to drop load by ~25%.

runtime-alejandra: attempting manual create hotshot pool with fastwarm flag: 
```
redwoodctl pools create --region us-west --type hotshot --fast-warm=true --size 2 --labels emergency
```
Started pool creation id=hotshot-em-001. currently WARMING.

infra-ops-bot: note: previous warmup code path requires full model fetch and kv preload; fast-warm aims to skip KV preload for streaming coldstarts.

oncall-jen: rerouting high-priority customers? we should avoid breaking SLAs. @product-mike any objections to temporary model downgrade (quantized variant) for enterprise for next 20m?

product-mike: ok for 20m as emergency; coordinate with CS to notify customers. prefer explicit opt-in only for impacted customers.

customer-success-sara: notifying customers now: "We are mitigating elevated latency by rerouting traffic and enabling temporary capacities. Expect improved performance within minutes. Updates in this thread."

monitoring-log: p99_streaming_latency: 12.6s -> 9.2s after PLG traffic reroute (5m window); queue_depth: 120 -> 88. not stable yet.

runtime-alejandra: hotshot-em-001 reported WARMUP_COMPLETE at 6250001250, added to pool ring. starting warmup bypass for first N requests.

sre-liam: after hotshot add, p99 dropped to ~6.8s for a short window then rose to ~8.5s. I suspect handshake/slot allocation race leading to bursts of WAIT_FOR_SLOT.

oncall-jen: digging into autoscaler backoff: seen backoff spike because several pool-create attempts failed due to healthcheck strictness (curl /health returned 503 until full KV load). That kept autoscaler from creating enough capacity quickly.

runtime-alejandra: root cause hypothesis: warmup policy requires KV preload and our KV store (nfs-cache) experienced transient latency spike, making the warmup step take 4x longer; autoscaler treats warmup as failing and throttles further creates (exponential backoff). combined with sudden demand (customer batch) -> queue depth surge.

sre-liam: confirm from logs: 
```
2026-03-15T10:27:09Z pool=pc-84f2 stage=WARMUP kv_load_time=78.4s status=degraded
2026-03-15T10:27:14Z autoscaler backoff factor=8 next_attempt_in=120s
```

infra-ops-bot: cluster infra alert: nfs-cache latency 300ms -> 2.4s spike at 10:25UTC (coincident). root cause: degraded nfs-controller pod restarted at 10:23 and reattached volumes slowly.

oncall-jen: immediate mitigations taken: 
- routed PLG -> hosted-fallback (done)
- manually created hotshot pool with fast-warm (done)
- temporarily increased autoscaler concurrency limit for us-west to allow 3 concurrent creates (now)
- evicted low-priority batch jobs (started)

sre-liam: manual scale command used: 
```
redwoodctl autoscaler update --region us-west --concurrent-create-limit 3
```

runtime-alejandra: note: increasing concurrent creates is a safety-risk if warmup keeps failing (could increase churn). added a short TTL: revert in 15m unless healthy.

monitoring-log: p99 now 4.9s, p95 1.8s, queue_depth 22. customer ticket volume decreased. streaming stalls count trending down.

product-mike: good, CS please keep customers updated. we should prepare a post-incident note and potential credit offers.

customer-success-sara: will update tickets and send a status email to impacted contacts.

oncall-jen: handoff: oncall-jen -> sre-liam taking lead for long tail investigation. will mark in pagerduty and create a followup runbook issue. any objections?

sre-liam: taking. will run root cause RCA and coordinate with infra to validate nfs-controller fixes.

runtime-alejandra: next steps I'm pushing now: 
- tighten warmup fallback: allow fast-warm for critical lanes automatically when KV latency > 500ms
- add autoscaler circuit-breaker to avoid exponential backoff when infra latencies detected
- instrument warmup success rate metric per pool with alerting threshold

noncall-jen: documenting quick timeline for postmortem: 
- 10:24UTC initial traffic surge; autoscaler warmup slow due to nfs-cache latency spike
- 10:25-10:31UTC p99 breaches, streaming stalls reported, customers ticketed
- 10:27-10:32UTC PLG reroute + manual hotshot pool + increase concurrent create -> partial mitigation
- 10:35UTC p99 within SLO at edge, complete recovery by 10:44UTC

product-mike: also capture potential mitigations from product side: per-customer throttle, queued prioritization for enterprise customers, and pre-warm reservations for scheduled batch jobs.

sre-liam: I'm creating an issue: "RCA: warmup slow due to nfs-cache latency -> autoscaler backoff + capacity starvation" with actions and owners. will attach logs and metrics.

customer-success-sara: final customer update drafted, will send once SRE confirms recovery.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> watches in place. incident duration ~20m. Labels: dedicated, warmup, autoscaler, nfs-cache.

sre-liam: closing on-call handoff. follow-ups: infra to harden nfs-controller restart path, runtime to implement fast-warm auto-trigger and remove strict full-kv requirement for initial streaming slots, product to explore reservation/pre-warm features.

oncall-jen: thanks team. tagging for postmortem sync in 24h. :thumbsup:
